purpose: Author original MathMaster generator families that train the mathematics and linguistic register students encounter on the current digital SAT without copying College Board items.

responseModes.rule: Preserve the SAT ecology at corpus/session level. Do not force every TEKS mapping to contain both formats when the skill does not naturally support both.

context.rule: Use science, social-science, or real-world context only when the context is mathematically functional. Avoid decorating every item with a story.

do: Use concise declarative setup followed by one precise mathematical question.

Use the vocabulary the construct requires: value, solution, equation, function, rate of change, y-intercept, equivalent, factor, percent, probability, sample, margin of error, radius, angle, volume, and other domain terms when mathematically appropriate.
State units next to quantities when units matter.
Let difficult items become difficult through mathematical structure, representation, inference, or multi-step dependence rather than through extra directions.
For student-produced response, ask for the mathematical result directly; the interface already communicates that the student must enter a response.
Build distractors from identifiable misconceptions or operation errors, not correctAnswer plus 1/2/3 unless those values genuinely model likely errors.
avoid: Select the best Digital SAT answer.
teacher-facing coaching inside the student prompt
globalLanguageRules.copyrightRule: Model assessment conventions and tested constructs; do not reproduce or lightly paraphrase proprietary question text from official banks.

officialSkillFamilies: systems of two linear equations in two variables
linear inequalities in one or two variables
register: Short symbolic setup is normal; do not force a word problem.
When a function is given, ask for a value, feature, equivalent representation, or interpretation that belongs to the official linear-function skill family.
For contextual linear models, define variables and units naturally and ask what a coefficient, value, solution, or equation means in that context.
Use graph/table language only when the item actually supplies that representation.
authenticTaskPatterns: equation or expression -> determine a solution/value
linear function -> determine or interpret slope/rate/intercept/output
two points/table/graph -> determine a linear relationship or feature
two linear relationships -> determine an intersection or parameter
linear inequality -> determine values or interpret the solution set

officialSkillFamilies: systems of equations in two variables
register: Use precise structural language such as equivalent, factor, zero, solution, maximum, minimum, coefficient, constant, exponential, quadratic, rational, radical, or polynomial only when it is the tested idea.
Harder items should require recognition of structure, reverse reasoning, parameter relationships, or linking representations—not a meta instruction to verify work.
Keep single-answer response behavior even when the reasoning is cognitively complex.
authenticTaskPatterns: expression -> identify an equivalent form that reveals a feature
nonlinear equation -> determine solution or parameter
nonlinear function -> determine or interpret a key feature
linear/nonlinear system -> determine an intersection or dependent quantity

officialSkillFamilies: ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
one-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
inference from sample statistics and margin of error
evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
register: Context is usually functional here. Name the population, sample, variable, unit, or study design when it matters.
Use statistically precise distinctions among sample and population, association and causation, random selection and random assignment, predicted and observed values, and center and spread.
Do not reduce data-analysis items to generic arithmetic wrapped in a story when the mapped skill calls for interpretation.
authenticTaskPatterns: data display/model -> determine or interpret a statistic/prediction
probability setting -> determine conditional or unconditional probability
sample/study -> determine supported inference or evaluate claim

register: State geometric relationships and units precisely; include a figure/diagram only when the runtime can actually render it.
Use coordinate-plane language when coordinates are part of the task, and conventional geometry vocabulary when it is necessary to reason.
Contextual geometry should require modeling a real dimension, angle, area, or volume rather than merely attaching a noun to a formula exercise.
authenticTaskPatterns: given dimensions/relationships -> determine length, area, or volume
angle/triangle relationships -> determine a missing measure
right triangle -> determine side/angle using similarity or trigonometry
circle equation/geometry -> determine radius, center, arc, angle, or related measure

challengeRules.minimum: Three independently authored challenge families per mapped standard before V2.1 can publish.
mustDifferFromDirectSource: task grammar when the mathematical construct permits it
forbidden: Clone a direct generator and only raise difficultyBand/DOK.
Create difficulty by prepending Challenge or a hypothetical wrong student/test taker.
Call an item DOK 3 solely because the prompt asks the student to verify or explain.

versioningRules.fidelityVersion: Set ccmrFidelity.version to 2.1 only after authentic-language and underlying-task audits pass.
versioningRules.contentRelease: Pin new sessions to the V2.1 content release. Preserve submitted evidence from older releases.
versioningRules.staleSessionPolicy: Do not hot-swap a student's unanswered questions across content releases. Retire stale active CCMR practice sessions at the release boundary and start a new session at the student's preserved progression tier. Secure exam simulations stay pinned to their original release.
